course_name_original: Masini unelte si prelucrări prin aschiere
course_name_en: CNC Machines Tools and Cutting Processing
prerequisites: Use of standardized symbols for functional diagrams in mechanics, electrical engineering, optics, pneumatics and hydraulics.
Application of technical drawing standards and conventional engineering graphic representations in the elaboration of execution drawings, technological sheets, product manuals, testing manuals, etc.

learning_outcomes.text: The student/graduate identifies and describes basic principles and methods of the mechanical engineering field.
Explains the fundamental elements of mechanical cutting processing.
Compares and analyzes the technological process of producing parts on various machine tools.

Evaluates the technological possibilities of performing processing operations on CNC machine tools (estimations of work types, errors in technological processing stages, evaluates the effects of errors in the MUSDP system).
Establishes the regime for parts that can be produced on various types of machine tools.
Uses CAD design and CAM programming concepts for CNC machine tools.
Applies cutting regimes for various classic or numerically controlled machine tools.
Establishes the type of tool for various part geometries.
Uses cutting regimes for tools used in the cutting process.
Establishes the transmission ratios of main and working movements in the cutting process.
The student/graduate operates with basic methods and techniques in the field and associates them with specific graphic representations of mechanical engineering.
Uses machine tools for various technological processes.
Establishes the necessary devices for orienting/positioning and fixing blanks for cutting processing.
Plans the technological process for producing parts by cutting.
Creates various surfaces generated on machine tools.
Evaluates the quality of surfaces generated after cutting processing.
The student/graduate selects and analyzes specific bibliographic sources in the field of mechanical engineering.

Respects the commitment to ethical principles, norms, and values in fulfilling professional tasks. This commitment is evidenced by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the work group and applies effective relationship and teamwork techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Demonstrates competence in integrating into the work group and applying techniques for building relationships and effective teamwork at different hierarchical levels.
To stay informed and up-to-date in their fields. This requires the judicious application of effective lifelong learning methodologies and techniques.
Develops professional projects in the field of engineering.

syllabus_topics: Cutting processing. Introductory notions in the field of cutting processing. Kinematics of the cutting process. Parameters of the cutting regime.
Generation of surfaces by turning. Methods and variants of generation by turning. Particularities of helical groove generation on a lathe.
Generation of surfaces by planing and slotting. Specific elements of planing and slotting surfaces. Methods and variants of generation by planing and slotting.

Generation of surfaces by drilling, reaming-countersinking, boring. Specific elements of surfaces by drilling, reaming-countersinking, and boring. Methods and variants of generation by drilling, reaming-countersinking, and boring.
Generation of surfaces by milling. Specific elements of surface generation by milling. Methods and variants of surface milling.

Generation of surfaces by abrasive machining. Specific elements of surface generation by abrasive machining. Abrasive machining of simple and compound plane surfaces. Abrasive machining of surfaces of revolution. Smoothing procedures. Superfinishing. Lapping. Honing.

Machine tool. Definition. Classification. Functions and requirements of the machine tool. Technological and user requirements. Basic mechanism. Structure of the machine tool. Foundation of the machine tool and types of foundations. Structural analysis. Structural components. Constructions. Materials. Modularity. Guiding systems. Guide constructions. Main kinematic chain. Main spindle. Main spindle constructions. Feed kinematic chains. Classification. Constructions. Component elements. Ball screw. Classification. Constructions. Analysis of feed chain operation. Tool clamping system. Cutting tool handling, transport, and storage system. Part clamping system.
Work safety; presentation of the laboratory and the machine tools to be used in training in the field of cutting processing.
Kinematics of the cutting processing.
Cutting tools.
Transmission mechanisms and transformation mechanisms.
Surface generation on the lathe. Kinematic construction of the normal lathe.
Thread cutting on the normal lathe.
Surface generation by milling. Construction and kinematics of the milling machine.
Use of devices on the milling machine.
Surface generation by planing. Construction and kinematics of the transverse planing machine.
Boring processing. Kinematic construction of the drilling machine.
Grinding of plane and revolution surfaces. Construction of the grinding machine.
Structure of the numerically controlled (CNC) machine tool.
Computer-aided programming of numerically controlled milling machines.
Catch-up for missed laboratory sessions.
teaching_methods: PowerPoint presentations based on course material
Discovery learning models facilitated by direct and indirect exploration of reality
Solving technological problems of part production by cutting

assessment_methods.method: Laboratory activities (completion of lab sheets and laboratory colloquium)

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. Minimum requirements for passing include identifying transmission and transformation mechanisms in classic machine tools, explaining working movements for mechanical cutting processes, recognizing component elements of a CNC machine, and explaining the functioning of machine tool systems.
